keywords: qteasy 数据从哪来到哪去
title: How qteasy data is organized
summary: Channels fill a local store; stable information ids are read through three doors; history-shaped series can become a HistoryPanel.
narrative:
qteasy's data path has three layers. Network channels fill a local store. The store holds cleaned tables. Stable information ids are then read through a small set of entry points, and history-shaped series can become a HistoryPanel. This card only names those layers. Downloading still needs an explicit date range and a confirmed Plan.

The numbers below name the next windows. A later question may refer to a number; explain that item from its card.

1. DataSource is the local store of predefined tables. overview and get_table_info show what is already there.
2. A data channel is the network source passed into refill. It is not a DataType and not a table.
3. Refill copies a bounded date range into the local store. Ask explains it; Plan performs it.
4. Before screening or type lookup, download the small starter set. This is not a catalog of every table.
5. Check the token and which local tables exist before a download.
6. Three read doors: history, reference, and static. get_kline is sugar on history, not a fourth door.
7. Screen a pool with static attributes, then pass the codes into a history read.
8. HistoryPanel is the in-memory shares × dates × series container for history-shaped data.

Numbered table catalogs in the manual are storage layouts, not cards here.
